subject: Critical: FastMerchant checkout interruptions — networking investigation
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@fastmerchant.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: netops@fastmerchant.com
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Elevated p50/p95 and intermittent 5xxs on checkout (prod)

Markus,

We started seeing checkout failures at 08:57 PDT — roughly 7-12% 5xx on our checkout flow and token p50 for our inference routes spiked from ~80ms to 1.2s. This is causing cart drop and multiple customers are reporting payment failures. Our SREs see a burst of DNS lookups to redwood inference endpoints and a corresponding rise in TCP retransmits.

Attached is a small error sample and a capture that our net team took. Can you confirm whether there were any model-side throttles or autoscaling activity that would explain the latency? We need an urgent workaround — can you pause routing to the primary peering or route to a fallback?

Thanks,
Amy Chen
VP Engineering, FastMerchant

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@fastmerchant.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com, netops@fastmerchant.com
Date: 2028-06-25T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p50/p95 and intermittent 5xxs on checkout (prod)

Amy — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. Initial check: no recent model tunings or autoscale events on the inference cluster that match this timing; platform CPU/GPU utilization is nominal and instance counts steady.

We see repeated DNS resolution attempts coming from a subset of FastMerchant IPs and some connection resets. Two immediate asks while we investigate:
- Can your net team temporarily reduce DNS TTLs to 30s for the affected records so we can test failover quicker?
- Can we try an immediate bypass: FastMerchant route a subset of production traffic to our secondary peering (ipsec-peer-2) for 15 minutes as a mitigation test?

I'm looping in Lauren (ops lead) and Rachel (customer success) so we can coordinate a rollback/communication plan. We'll share a short exec brief in the next 90 minutes.

— Markus Klein
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: inference-failover-playbook.pdf (see step-by-step failover runbook)

From: Network Ops <netops@fastmerchant.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Amy Chen <amy.chen@fastmerchant.com>
Cc: Tim Harper <tim.harper@fastmerchant.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p50/p95 and intermittent 5xxs on checkout (prod)

On Mon, Jun 25, 2028 at 09:30 Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can your net team temporarily reduce DNS TTLs to 30s for the affected records so we can test failover quicker?

We can lower TTLs but wanted to add visibility: we are seeing asymmetry on the peering to the east coast POP — some sessions are being hairpinned through a 3rd-party firewall cluster at our cloud provider region which is intermittently dropping SYN+ACKs and triggering retransmits. Also noticed NXDOMAIN/ SERVFAIL flapping from one of our resolvers after failures. We'll try lowering the TTLs; starting that now and preparing policy to shift 10% of traffic to ipsec-peer-2. Will confirm when route is live.

— NetOps

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-25T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: FastMerchant — network escalation & exec brief draft

Team — internal note and proposed exec text. Please review and suggest edits before I send to Vivek for visibility.

Summary (for execs):
- Impact: FastMerchant checkout flow experienced ~7–12% 5xx and p50 increased to 1.2s between 08:55–10:30 PDT for ~2 hours.
- Preliminary cause: asymmetric peering via customer cloud firewall + resolver TTL churn causing excessive DNS lookups and TCP retransmits; observed proxy session resets and elevated connection latency to inference endpoints.
- Immediate mitigations: FastMerchant routing 10% traffic to secondary peer (ipsec-peer-2) + lowered DNS TTLs; Redwood enabling a temporary bypass for inference traffic from the affected FastMerchant IP block to avoid proxy traversal.
- Next steps: joint postmortem, adjust peer health checks, consider longer TTLs stabilization and a config to avoid hairpinning through customer-middleboxes.

Proposed message to FastMerchant execs (short):
"Vivek — we’re treating this as high priority. Our engineers and FastMerchant SREs have identified an asymmetric peering path and intermittent firewall-induced connection resets that are amplifying DNS churn. We’ve implemented a controlled failover to the secondary peering and a DNS TTL reduction to mitigate. We are monitoring closely and will share an update in 30 minutes with timelines for full recovery and compensation options."

Please flag any inaccuracies. I also attached the playbook with runbook steps to ensure we won't blow up the rest of the region.

— Lauren
Director, Platform Operations

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@fastmerchant.com>, netops@fastmerchant.com
Date: 2028-06-26T16:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Critical: FastMerchant checkout interruptions — networking investigation

Thanks for the quick coordination and the clear summary. A few asks from leadership:
1) Provide a one-page exec timeline by EOD PT that includes customer impact metrics (orders impacted, estimated revenue at risk) and the exact mitigation actions taken.
2) Confirm whether we should proactively offer a billing credit and what level — Ops suggests a 7-day credit for the affected window; Sales may want to negotiate.
3) Long-term: start a cross-functional engineering project to add active-path probes and a peering-policy objective that prevents hairpinning via 3rd-party firewalls. Include cost estimate and target SLT.

Operational note: Our preliminary root cause looks like this chain — (a) edge resolver timeout at customer side causes repeated client-side lookups, (b) failover/peering asymmetry pushes traffic through a noisy firewall cluster that intermittently drops packets, (c) the dropped packets cause session resets and elevate p50 and error rates. We should capture full packet traces and BPF logs for the final postmortem.

Markus/Team — please produce the one-pager and a proposed credit band for the finance/sales review. Rachel, work with Amy to line up a customer update that balances transparency and reassurance.

— Vivek Kulkarni
CTO, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: redwood-debug-logs-20280625.zip, fastmerchant-error-sample-20280625.json
